Dates use the relative tokens documented in lib/mock/mock_date_resolver.dart

entries.headline: The quiet win at the end of a loud week
entries.content:
Nothing about this week looked like progress from the outside. Four days of meetings that could have been notes, a migration that rolled back twice, and a laptop that decided Thursday was a good day to forget my keyboard layout.

Then at nine tonight the last check went green and the room went quiet in a good way. I sat with it for a minute before telling anyone, which is new for me. Usually I broadcast the win before I have felt it.

Writing it down so that next time the week is loud I remember it can still end like this.

entries.headline: Team dinner after the v2 launch
entries.content:
Twelve of us around a table built for eight. Priya ordered for the whole group without asking anyone and somehow got it exactly right.

The part I want to keep: Daniel raising a glass to the people who wrote the migration scripts nobody will ever see. That is the kind of credit that does not usually make it to the toast.

entries.headline: Six kilometres before sunrise
entries.content:
Out the door before I could argue with myself about it. The road by the reservoir still had last night's rain on it and the light came up somewhere around the fourth kilometre.

No music today. Just the sound of my own pace settling down after the first ten minutes, which is the part I always forget is coming.

entries.headline: Couldn't sleep, so I mapped the whole year
entries.content:
Two in the morning, notebook on the floor, every quarter sketched out in a handwriting that got worse as the hours went on.

Most of it will not survive contact with reality and I know that. But there is something about laying the whole thing out end to end that makes the next two weeks feel smaller instead of larger.

entries.headline: Coastal hike with Ravi and Meera
entries.content:
Fourteen kilometres of ridge with the sea on our left the entire way. Ravi brought a thermos of coffee that had gone cold by the first viewpoint and we drank it anyway.

We stopped talking somewhere around the halfway mark and stayed quiet for almost an hour. Three people who have known each other for a decade, walking, saying nothing, and none of it awkward.

Best day in months and it cost us a tank of fuel and a packet of biscuits.

entries.headline: Rewrote the onboarding in one sitting
entries.content:
Four hours, one pot of tea, no notifications. The whole flow came apart and went back together as three screens instead of seven.

I have been circling this for a month. It turns out the thing blocking me was not the problem, it was never giving myself an afternoon where nothing else was allowed to be urgent.

entries.headline: Anniversary dinner, table by the window
entries.content:
Same restaurant, same table, ninth year running. The owner recognised us before we said the name on the booking, which is either lovely or a sign we are extremely predictable.

We spent most of it talking about the year ahead rather than the one behind. That felt like the right direction.

entries.headline: A slow Sunday and nothing to prove
entries.content:
Woke without an alarm. Read on the balcony until the sun came round far enough to make it uncomfortable, then moved inside and kept reading.

Did not open a laptop. Did not make a list. The whole day came to about six hundred words of a book and two cups of coffee, and I am counting it as a good one.

entries.headline: Live set at the Old Tram Shed
entries.content:
A room for two hundred with maybe ninety people in it, which turned out to be the right number. The band played the second album front to back with no gap between tracks.

Stood near the back with Nadia, both of us pretending we were too old for the front and both of us wrong about that.

entries.headline: The deadline moved and so did I
entries.content:
Third time the date has shifted and the second time nobody told the people doing the work until the day of.

I wrote a long message, deleted it, and wrote a short one instead. The short one got a reply in four minutes. Noting that for next time, because the long one would have felt better to send and done nothing.

entries.headline: Moving day: forty-two boxes, one surviving plant
entries.content:
Started at six, finished at nine at night, ate standing up in a kitchen with no chairs yet.

The monstera made it. The one I have moved four times and nearly killed twice. Everything else is replaceable and I would like the record to show I know that.

entries.headline: Finished the Le Guin, started it again
entries.content:
Closed it, sat there for a while, then opened it at page one the same evening. I have done that with maybe four books.

What gets me is how little of it is spent explaining itself. It just builds the place and trusts you to keep up.

entries.headline: First day at the new desk
entries.content:
Arrived forty minutes early because I could not judge the commute, then sat in a cafe across the road pretending that was the plan.

By the afternoon I had a laptop, a badge that did not work, and the names of about nine people I will absolutely have to ask again.

entries.headline: Three in the morning and the city is finally quiet
entries.content:
Could not sleep again. Sat by the window and watched the one delivery bike that seems to run this street at this hour.

Some nights the quiet is restful and some nights it is just empty. Tonight it was the second one. Writing it down anyway, because the rule I made was that I write the flat days too.

entries.headline: The rooftop birthday
entries.content:
Somebody strung lights across the whole terrace and nobody will admit to organising it. Twenty-odd people, one speaker that kept disconnecting, and a cake that arrived an hour late and got eaten anyway.

This is the one I think about when someone asks what a good night looks like.

entries.headline: The morning I decided to start writing this down
entries.content:
Two years ago today. A cheap notebook, a train that was late, and the sudden and slightly embarrassing realisation that I could not account for most of the previous year.

Not the big things. Those I remember. The ordinary Tuesdays had just gone, and there had been a few hundred of them.

entries.headline: The conversation I keep rehearsing
entries.content:
Ran the numbers three times and then ran the conversation five times in my head, which is four more than useful.

The facts are fine. It is the asking that I keep stalling on.

entries.headline: A letter I will probably never send
entries.content:
Wrote four paragraphs to someone who has not spoken to me in two years, then sat and looked at it.

It says what I would want it to say. That might be enough on its own.

entries.headline: Session nine
entries.content:
We went back to the thing from session two and it landed completely differently this time.

Homework for the fortnight: notice when I am managing the room instead of being in it.
